newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: ING rates Slovak refiner long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: ING rates Slovak refiner long-term buy.

text.p: ING Barings rates shares of Slovakia's sole oil refiner, Slovnaft a.s., a long-term buy, saying the issue is significantly undervalued.

Slovnaft's share price has risen sharply over the past weeks to close at 990 crowns on Monday, but Vladimir Zlacky of ING Barings said the issue's 16.5 percent rise this year did not change his outlook.

"I would keep the (long-term buy) recommendation despite the recent increase in the issue's price, as the company's shares are still significantly undervalued compared with similar producers in the region," he said.

ING said in an investor report that, in a "conservative sum-of-the-parts valuation" Slovnaft's share price should be 1,091 crowns, while on price to earnings ratio grounds, the share is rated at around half the level of similar refineries in central Europe.
"We believe that shareholders should take advantage of current weakness to buy for the long term," the report said.

The main bases for the recommendation were Slovnaft's strong position on domestic and neighbouring markets, heavy investment programmes to boost production and the expected rapid growth in petrol demand in its target countries.
In 1994, Slovnaft bought a majority stake in then state- owned petrol distributor Benzinol, giving the group a 66 percent share of the domestic retail market.
The company also announced plans to build its own petrol station chain in southern Poland and expand its 25-strong chain in the eastern part of the Czech Republic.

ING cites a General Motors forecast as saying car ownership in eastern Europe should rise by some 80 percent over the next decade, providing a base for a sharp increase in petrol consumption in the region in coming years.

The government's willingness to adjust domestic motor fuel prices to the development of the world crude oil markets, enabling Slovnaft to reduce cyclical margin swings, is also cited as a reason for optimism, the report said. Last year the finance ministry approved five petrol price hikes.
